name: White Chocolate Caramel Protein Cookies
description: White chocolate caramel spin on the excellent-rated Browned-Butter Protein Cookies base (same dough: browned butter 15 g, brown sugar 28 g chew, whey 40 g, 3 tall mounds). Mix-ins swap semi-sweet for white chocolate baking chunks (15 g, a couple pressed on top to toast golden) + toffee bits (10 g, folded toward the center for chewy caramel pockets); finished with a zero-cal SF caramel drizzle at serving (the syrup never sets - never drizzle for storage). Also the FIRST xanthan-in-a-cookie test: 1/8 tsp whisked into the dry for bendy chew - gummy or bouncy means the gum comes out; a real chew win graduates it to the other cookie bases. ~253 cal | 16.2P per cookie, ratio ~15.6 (fat ~32% of cals - candy-loaded by design). To-make.

payload.instructionText: Serve: drizzle each cookie with ~1 tsp sugar-free caramel syrup just before eating - microwave the cookie 8-10 sec first for a warm, gooey bite.

Whisk the xanthan gum into the whey, flour, and pudding mix while everything is still dry - NEVER straight into the wet, or it pearls into slime beads. Add dry: stir the whey-flour-pudding-xanthan blend, baking soda, and salt into the wet until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the white chocolate chunks and toffee bits. It should hold its shape, not pour. Too stiff/dry -> a splash of milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Taste for sweetness.
Shape into 3 tall mounds - do NOT flatten. Press a chunk or two of white chocolate onto the top of each mound for the bakery look; they'll toast golden in the oven.

payload.text: First xanthan test in a cookie: 1/8 tsp for the batch, whisked into the dry. It's the chew lever Splenda can't provide - bendy, cohesive, moist instead of crumbly - stacked on the brown sugar's dissolved-sugar chew. Escalation: gummy/slick -> drop it next round; bouncy -> that's the gum stacking with the whey's elasticity, xanthan comes out of cookies. If the chew genuinely improves, it graduates to the other cookie bases. Never exceed 1/4 tsp per batch.

Toffee bits that end up at a mound's edge melt out and re-set as brittle caramel lace on the tray - tasty but fragile. Fold them toward the center of the dough so they bake into chewy caramel pockets inside the cookie instead.
White chocolate scorches faster than semi-sweet - the pressed-on chunks should toast golden (a butterscotch bonus), but don't run long; blackened white chocolate turns bitter.
The SF caramel syrup is thin and never sets - drizzle at serving only. Drizzled ahead, it soaks in and the cookies go sticky/soggy in storage.
